page.notes: The Hebrew word after "sed tantum" is printed in a worn fount; my reading אביב is doubtful and is marked [?]. The Greek "Φεγγαρίς" is copied as printed. The last word of the page, "Lon-", breaks at the line end; its completion "go" is the catchword. Long s has been written as plain s throughout, and u/v and i/j normalised as instructed (e.g. "qvæ" to "quæ", "eamqve" to "eamque", "liqvebit" to "liquebit"). The printed "Successoribus" keeps its capital S.
